newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK BANK MULLS SUBORDINATED DEBT ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK BANK MULLS SUBORDINATED DEBT ISSUE.

text.p: Vseobecna Uverova Banka a.s. (VUB), Slovakia's largest commercial bank, said on Thursday it is mulling an international subordinated debt issue to help raise its basic capital.
The announcement comes a month after VUB's rival, savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna, said it was mulling a similar issue which would be the first of its kind in central Europe.
"We will mandate one financial institution to lead-manage and issue our subordinated debt abroad in the near future," Jozef Galis, Director of VUB's Foreign Exchange Relations Division, told Reuters.

Galis added that the end of the year seemed like a "very short" time off. He said the bank has been in touch with several international institutions, and was still discussing the issue's basic details.
"Any detail is premature at this stage," he said.
"This is one way how to restructure our bank, though it does not solve everything, only the capital increase," he added, declining to say how large the issue needed to be.
VUB has the largest capital base of any bank in Slovakia, with basic capital totalling 4.1 billion crowns.
Two weeks ago, VUB president Jan Gabriel, said the bank needed to at least double its capital, but it would have to first stabilise the situation of its risky assets.
The debt issue volume would also be determined by the Slovak central bank, which must approve any such programme, Galis added.

"But the issue should include Eurobonds, and their issuance is a problem since Slovak securitites law does not really allow for it. However, it can be legally solved though not easily," Galis added, not specifying further.
A month ago, Moody's Investors Service assigned to VUB ratings of Ba1 for long-term deposits, not prime for short-term deposits, and D for financial strength.

However, Moody's said the ratings also recognise VUB's high level of classified loans, its loan loss provision inadequacy, its reduced but considerable dependence on interbank funding, its moderate preprovision profitability.
VUB's solvency ratio hit 4.8 percent at the 1995-end.
